papers.title: Progress in anticancer chemical constituents and pharmacological research of Carpesium cernuum L. (Review).
papers.abstract: The present study aimed to systematically review the anticancer chemical constituents, pharmacological effects, and molecular targets of Carpesium cernuum L., clarify the molecular network of its anticancer mechanisms, summarize the research achievements and limitations and provide a scientific reference for its development and utilization, the research and development of novel anticancer drugs, and clinical applications. Through literature collation and experimental data integration, the chemical constituents of C. cernuum were classified and identified, and with the aid of in vitro cell expe
papers.summary: This review compiles the anticancer chemical constituents and pharmacological effects of Carpesium cernuum L., a medicinal plant, integrating literature and experimental data to map its molecular targets and mechanism network. It summarizes current research achievements and limitations to guide future drug development and clinical application of the plant's bioactive compounds.

papers.title: Impact of EEG-related HPO terms on phenotype-driven variant prioritization in pediatric epilepsy.
papers.abstract: The Human Phenotype Ontology (HPO) is a standardized resource of hierarchically organized phenotypic terms used for deep phenotyping, both in research and diagnosis. In our study, we aimed to investigate how the specificity of EEG-related HPO terms may impact phenotype and gene scoring and prioritization.
papers.summary: This study examines how the specificity of EEG-related Human Phenotype Ontology (HPO) terms affects phenotype-driven gene scoring and variant prioritization in pediatric epilepsy. The authors find that using more specific EEG terms can alter prioritization outcomes, highlighting the importance of precise phenotyping for diagnostic yield.

papers.title: OMA orthology in 2027: orthology, ancestral gene repertoires, and comparative genomics at scale.
papers.abstract: OMA is a longstanding resource for inferring and exploring orthologous relationships across the tree of life. Here, we describe recent developments that broaden the comparative genomics information and analyses supported by the OMA ecosystem. The latest OMA release contains 2983 extant genomes and 1226 ancestral genome reconstructions spanning all domains of life, with expanded eukaryotic representation and quality-assessed genome selection. We integrated protein structure-aware information across all proteins in OMA, providing structure-derived 3Di representations and structural alignments fo
papers.summary: OMA 2027 expands its orthology resource to 2,983 extant genomes and 1,226 reconstructed ancestral genomes across all domains of life, with improved eukaryotic coverage and quality-assessed genome selection. The update adds protein structure-aware information, including 3Di representations and structural alignments for all OMA proteins, enabling comparative genomics at scale.

papers.title: LACA: a cross-species single-cell resource for exploring longevity and aging-associated cellular and molecular programs.
papers.abstract: Different species can have various maximum lifespans, some with exceptional longevity, yet the underlying cellular and molecular mechanisms remain poorly understood. Despite rapid advances in single-cell transcriptomics, resources that systematically connect single-cell gene expression profiles to species lifespan are limited. We hereby present the Longevity & Aging Cell Atlas (LACA), a database that integrates single-cell transcriptomic datasets across 134 species with their maximum lifespans. LACA includes over 148 million cells with 190 annotated cell types from single-cell datasets. LACA a
papers.summary: LACA is a new database that integrates single-cell transcriptomic datasets from 134 species with information on their maximum lifespans, totaling over 148 million cells and 190 annotated cell types. It enables cross-species comparisons of cellular and molecular programs associated with longevity and aging. The resource aims to help researchers uncover mechanisms underlying exceptional longevity.

papers.title: De Novo Genome Assembly and Annotation of the Barbary Macaque (Macaca sylvanus), an Endangered Primate Endemic to North Africa.
papers.abstract: Background: The Barbary macaque (Macaca sylvanus) is the only macaque native to Africa, with a range restricted to the Atlas Mountains of Morocco and Algeria. The species is listed as Endangered by the IUCN, and no reference genome has previously been published, limiting both comparative work within Macaca and genome-scale study of the species itself. Methods: Here, we present a scaffold-level de novo draft genome assembly of M. sylvanus generated using a hybrid approach combining Oxford Nanopore long reads and Illumina short reads. Results: The final assembly spans 2.91 Gb across 9752 contigs
papers.summary: This paper reports the first de novo draft genome assembly for the Barbary macaque (Macaca sylvanus), an endangered primate endemic to North Africa, using a hybrid of Oxford Nanopore long reads and Illumina short reads. The scaffold-level assembly spans 2.91 Gb across 9,752 contigs, filling a gap in Macaca comparative genomics and enabling genome-scale study of this endangered species.

papers.title: PRGdb 5.0: a multi-layered resource for plant resistance gene discovery and exploration.
papers.abstract: Plant Resistance Genes database (PRGdb) 5.0 (https://prgdb.org/prgdb5/) is a major update of the PRGdb, designed to expand plant disease resistance gene resources within a unified web platform. The release incorporates predictions for 97 plant proteomes and adds 288, 315 new putative resistance-associated proteins, bringing the database to 874,967 candidate resistance proteins from 279 plant proteomes. The curated reference collection increased from 199 to 462 experimentally supported resistance proteins. To complement domain-based classification, the platform introduces an AI-assisted priorit
papers.summary: PRGdb 5.0 is a major update to a database of plant disease resistance genes, now covering 279 plant proteomes and 874,967 candidate resistance proteins, including 462 experimentally validated ones. The release adds AI-assisted prioritization of candidates and expands the resource into a unified web platform for resistance gene discovery.

papers.title: The mOTUs-db in 2027: linking taxonomy, genome-encoded function, and biogeography across environments.
papers.abstract: A molecular understanding of microbial communities requires linking taxonomic composition to the genome-resolved functional potential of member taxa. However, this integration remains challenging since representative genomes from cultivated strains are unavailable. Here, we present a new release of the mOTUs database, which extends genome coverage of underexplored environments and enriches its 3.9 million genome collection with functional annotations. Samples are annotated with a new hierarchical environmental ontology and geographic coordinates, supporting customizable sample grouping and bio
papers.summary: The mOTUs database has been updated to version 2027, expanding genome coverage for understudied environments and adding functional annotations to its 3.9 million genomes. It also introduces a hierarchical environmental ontology and geographic coordinates for samples, enabling customizable grouping and biogeographic analysis that links taxonomy to genome-encoded function across environments.

papers.title: Machine Learning-Based Prediction of Abiotic Stress-Responsive Genes in Date Palm (Phoenix dactylifera L.).
papers.abstract: Abiotic stresses pose major constraints to Phoenix dactylifera L. productivity in different environments. Although date palm possesses substantial adaptive capacity, experimentally validated stress-responsive gene resources remain limited. Here, we developed a sequence-based machine learning framework to prioritize candidate abiotic stress-responsive genes in date palm. Training labels were derived computationally: the 48,801-protein reference proteome was annotated by best-hit orthology to Arabidopsis thaliana, and stress-associated Gene Ontology terms transferred from these orthologs were us
papers.summary: The authors built a sequence-based machine learning framework to prioritize candidate abiotic stress-responsive genes in date palm, using stress-associated Gene Ontology terms transferred from Arabidopsis orthologs as training labels across the 48,801-protein reference proteome. This provides a computational route to expand limited experimentally validated stress-gene resources in a non-model crop.

papers.title: Transcriptome-Wide Profiling of lncRNAs and mRNAs Provides an Exploratory Interaction Catalogue for Skeletal Muscle Development and Fat-Tail Deposition in Bashibay and Argali × Bashibay Crossbred Sheep.
papers.abstract: Long noncoding RNAs (lncRNAs) have emerged as important post-transcriptional contributors to adipogenesis and myogenesis, yet their coordinated expression programs in sheep skeletal muscle and fat-tail tissue remain largely uncharacterised. In the present study, strand-specific RNA sequencing was applied to biceps brachii and tail-fat samples from three Bashibay ewes and three Argali × Bashibay F2 crossbred ewes, yielding 1,372,578,535 clean reads across twelve libraries. A stringent pipeline integrating CNCI, CPC, and Pfam identified 2755 lncRNA transcripts (834 known, 1921 novel) alongside 2
papers.summary: This study used strand-specific RNA sequencing to profile long noncoding RNAs (lncRNAs) and mRNAs in skeletal muscle and fat-tail tissue from Bashibay sheep and Argali × Bashibay crossbred sheep. The authors identified 2,755 lncRNA transcripts (834 known, 1,921 novel) and built an exploratory catalogue of lncRNA–mRNA interactions potentially involved in muscle development and fat-tail deposition. The work provides a resource for future functional studies of lncRNAs in sheep meat and fat traits.

papers.title: Function Without Closure: Navigating the Conceptual Diversity of Protein Annotation Databases.
papers.abstract: Assigning function to a protein is central to advancing our knowledge of living systems, yet the concept of "function" itself resists a single and stable definition. Sequence, structure, contextual and proteoform data continue to accumulate at pace, giving rise to an amount of annotation databases, but what counts as a protein's function shifts with context-a challenge that is as conceptual as it is technical. In this review, we discuss several approaches to defining biological function, and examine how these models are implemented in contemporary functional annotation databases. Differences i
papers.summary: This review examines how different conceptual definitions of protein "function" are implemented across contemporary functional annotation databases. It argues that what counts as a protein's function shifts with context—sequence, structure, proteoform, and other data types—making annotation a conceptual as well as technical challenge. The authors survey several models of biological function and compare how databases operationalize them.

papers.title: A multi-layer, multi-species graph-based framework for comparative analysis of sRNA-mediated regulation.
papers.abstract: Small RNAs (sRNAs) are central post-transcriptional regulators of bacterial gene expression, yet their evolutionary dynamics remain difficult to resolve due to limited sequence conservation. While sequence-homologous sRNAs can retain or diverge in function, unrelated sRNAs may independently evolve to regulate similar biological processes, making functional conservation invisible to sequence-based approaches. Here, we present a multi-layer, multi-species graph-based framework that integrates experimentally detected sRNA-messenger RNA interactions, orthology relationships, functional annotations
papers.summary: The authors present a graph-based computational framework that integrates experimentally detected sRNA–mRNA interactions, orthology relationships, and functional annotations across multiple bacterial species to enable comparative analysis of sRNA-mediated regulation. This approach addresses the challenge that sRNA sequence conservation is often too limited to reveal functional conservation, allowing detection of both homologous and convergently evolved regulatory relationships.

papers.title: CellStressDB: an AI-powered database of cellular responses to physical stressors.
papers.abstract: Physical stressors profoundly influence cellular behavior by triggering coordinated stress-response programs that regulate signaling, gene expression, metabolism, and cell fate. Here, we present CellStressDB (https://cellstressdb.omic.tech), an AI-powered database for exploring cellular responses to physical stressors. The current release contains data from 131 transcriptomic studies, with 2 364 816 cell and 1205 bulk sample observations from human and mouse across nine physical-stress classes and 21 tissue categories. Data and analyses are organized into 2848 indexed analysis entries across 7
papers.summary: CellStressDB is a new AI-powered database that compiles transcriptomic data on how cells respond to physical stressors, drawing from 131 studies and over 2.3 million single-cell plus 1,205 bulk observations across human and mouse. It covers nine physical-stress classes and 21 tissue categories, organized into 2,848 indexed analysis entries to support exploration of stress-response programs.

papers.title: A Graded Immune-Cell-Resolved cis-eQTL Mendelian Randomisation Screen Across Systemic Lupus Erythematosus and Related Immune Phenotypes.
papers.abstract: Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) is a genetically complex autoimmune disease. Whole-blood expression quantitative trait locus (eQTL) analyses capture average regulatory effects across leukocytes, whereas SLE involves immune processes that depend on cell context. Therefore, a cell-resolved screen requires rigorous verification of instrument identity, allele orientation, and the multiple-testing denominator before biological interpretation.
papers.summary: This study performs a cell-type-resolved cis-eQTL Mendelian randomisation screen to identify gene regulatory effects underlying systemic lupus erythematosus and related immune phenotypes, moving beyond whole-blood averages that obscure leukocyte-specific regulation. The authors emphasise rigorous quality control of instrument identity, allele orientation, and multiple-testing correction before biological interpretation. The work provides a framework for immune-cell-context-aware causal inference in autoimmune genetics.

papers.title: An Integrated Multi-Ontology Approach for Prioritizing Candidate Neurodevelopmental Disorder Genes.
papers.abstract: Rare neurodevelopmental disorders (NDDs) are clinically and genetically heterogeneous conditions affecting brain function, and a comprehensive set of NDD-associated genes is still lacking. We integrated gene lists from Orphanet, SFARI Gene, GeneTrek, and a large-scale genomic study, and classified 19,354 human protein-coding genes into 2639 high-confidence genes, 6856 candidate genes, and 9859 genes with no NDD evidence. Enrichment analysis of the high-confidence set highlighted nervous system development, synaptic processes, tRNA aminoacylation, and cancer-related pathways, and Monarch Diseas
papers.summary: The authors integrated gene lists from Orphanet, SFARI Gene, GeneTrek, and a large-scale genomic study to classify 19,354 human protein-coding genes into high-confidence, candidate, and no-evidence tiers for neurodevelopmental disorders. Enrichment analysis of the high-confidence set highlighted nervous system development, synaptic processes, tRNA aminoacylation, and cancer-related pathways. This provides a prioritized gene resource for NDD research and diagnosis.

papers.title: PDBe in 2027: integrating literature annotations, molecular dynamics data, and AI-ready access.
papers.abstract: The Protein Data Bank in Europe (PDBe; pdbe.org) provides open access to experimentally determined biomacromolecular structures and enriches these data with biological and functional context. Here, we describe recent developments that expand the information connected to PDB structures and introduce new ways for researchers and computational tools to access it. Literature integration has been extended to additional open-access publications, substantially increasing the availability of residue-level annotations mined from the scientific literature. Cross-links to molecular dynamics simulations i
papers.summary: PDBe has expanded its structural database to include residue-level annotations mined from more open-access literature, cross-links to molecular dynamics simulation data, and new access methods designed for AI and computational tools. These updates make it easier for both researchers and automated systems to connect PDB structures with functional and dynamic context.

papers.title: Ectopic Expression of SbNRT1.1A from Sorghum Improves Growth Under Low Nitrogen and Alters Nitrogen-Carbon-Related Gene Expression in Rice.
papers.abstract: Excessive application of nitrogen (N) fertilizers in modern agriculture causes serious environmental problems. Sorghum is recognized as a crop with high tolerance to low-fertility soil; however, the molecular mechanisms underlying its nitrate uptake and utilization remain largely unclear. In this study, we identified the sorghum putative nitrate transporter (NRT) gene SbNRT1.1A (Sobic.007G044300), and we generated two independent SbNRT1.1A-overexpression lines (OE-A1 and OE-A2) using the rice cultivar ZH11. Compared with wild-type (WT) plants, the OE lines exhibited significantly improved grow
papers.summary: The authors identified a sorghum nitrate transporter gene, SbNRT1.1A, and overexpressed it in rice. Transgenic rice lines grew better than wild-type plants under low nitrogen conditions and showed altered expression of genes related to nitrogen and carbon metabolism. This suggests SbNRT1.1A could be useful for engineering crops with improved nitrogen-use efficiency.

papers.title: Integrated Analysis of GWAS and Multi-Layer Molecular QTL Data Prioritizes Candidate Cis-Regulatory Mechanisms Underlying Semen Quality Traits in Pigs.
papers.abstract: Semen quality traits represent high-priority targets for the genetic improvement of boar reproductive efficiency. This study applied transcriptome-wide Mendelian randomization (TWMR) to systematically integrate genome-wide association study (GWAS) summary statistics with multi-layer molecular quantitative trait loci (molQTLs) from testis tissue, aiming to uncover the post-transcriptional regulatory architecture governing porcine semen quality. We collected 14,224 phenotypic records of six semen quality traits from 222 boars across four commercial breeds, with estimated heritabilities ranging f
papers.journal: Animals : an open access journal from MDPI
papers.summary: This study integrates pig GWAS summary statistics for semen quality traits with multi-layer molecular QTL data from testis tissue using transcriptome-wide Mendelian randomization (TWMR) to identify candidate cis-regulatory mechanisms. By combining 14,224 phenotypic records from 222 boars across four commercial breeds with molecular QTL layers, the authors prioritize regulatory variants and genes underlying boar reproductive traits. The work demonstrates how molQTL-informed MR can move from GWAS associations toward mechanistic regulatory hypotheses in livestock genetics.

papers.title: ONITH: An ontology-based non-clinical integration and term harmonization pipeline for data reuse in 3R.
papers.abstract: Animal studies continue to play a critical role in drug development as they uniquely capture the physiological complexity required to elucidate drug mechanisms and safety profiles. However, in alignment with the 3R principles (Reduce, Refine, Replace), there is a growing ethical and regulatory commitment to minimizing animal use. As part of this effort, the reuse of existing data has emerged as a potential strategy to support the transition toward more data-driven approaches in drug development, a direction that is increasingly supported by regulatory authorities as a viable alternative to ani
papers.journal: Computer methods and programs in biomedicine
papers.summary: ONITH is a pipeline that integrates non-clinical animal study data and harmonizes terminology using ontologies, aiming to make existing animal data more reusable in line with the 3R principles (Reduce, Refine, Replace). By standardizing terms across heterogeneous sources, it supports data-driven drug development while reducing the need for new animal experiments.

papers.title: Multi-omics-constrained kinetic models quantify pathway rewiring and predict metabolic vulnerabilities in BRCA1-deficient ovarian cancer.
papers.abstract: Time-resolved, network-wide consequences of cancer metabolic reprogramming remain poorly understood. We built multi-omics-constrained, near-genome-scale kinetic ensembles for isogenic BRCA1 wild-type and BRCA1-mutant ovarian cancer cells. Covering over 2,100 reactions, the ensembles enabled uncertainty-quantified simulations of nutrient, metabolite, and enzyme perturbations. Metabolic control analysis identified 28 enzyme-mediated vulnerabilities; 24 are linked to experimental or approved DrugBank compounds, whereas four lack documented drug associations. Independent DepMap data supported a su
papers.summary: The authors built near-genome-scale kinetic models of metabolism (over 2,100 reactions) constrained by multi-omics data for isogenic BRCA1 wild-type and BRCA1-mutant ovarian cancer cells. Using these models, they simulated nutrient, metabolite, and enzyme perturbations and identified 28 enzyme-mediated metabolic vulnerabilities, 24 of which map to existing or approved drugs. Independent DepMap data supported the predictions, suggesting the approach can prioritize druggable metabolic targets in BRCA1-deficient cancers.

papers.title: PANTHER: the protein tree and function resource in 2027.
papers.abstract: PANTHER (Protein ANalysis THrough Evolutionary Relationships) is a comprehensive resource of phylogenetic trees of protein-coding gene families. Trees are manually annotated with Gene Ontology (GO) terms describing how protein functional characteristics were gained and lost over time along tree branches, and these evolutionary models are used to create GO annotations for protein-coding genes. Orthologs, paralogs, and xenologs are assigned based on the trees. Here, we describe updates to the PANTHER resource since our previous published report in 2022. Since that time, the content of the databa
papers.summary: PANTHER is a database of phylogenetic trees for protein-coding gene families, with branches manually annotated using Gene Ontology terms to model how protein functions evolved. These evolutionary models are used to propagate GO annotations to genes and to classify orthologs, paralogs, and xenologs. This paper reports updates to the resource since its 2022 publication.

papers.title: PIANO enables generative modeling of gene expression and scales multi-omics integration to 100 million cells.
papers.abstract: Single-cell RNA technologies enable the routine acquisition of transcriptomic atlases. However, these molecular profiles are influenced by overlapping sources of variation. Since these covariates confound comparisons, data integration is the first step in most analyses. Three challenges remain: correcting strong batch effects, scaling to millions of cells, and modeling how covariates influence gene expression. To address these challenges, we developed PIANO, probabilistic inference autoencoder networks for multi-omics, a deep learning framework whose central feature is a generative model of ge
papers.summary: PIANO is a deep learning framework that uses a generative model of gene expression to integrate single-cell multi-omics data. It addresses three key challenges in data integration: correcting strong batch effects, scaling to millions of cells (demonstrated up to 100 million), and explicitly modeling how covariates influence gene expression. This enables more accurate comparisons across large-scale transcriptomic atlases.

papers.title: gcPathogen 2.0: an expanded multi-omics database advancing global pathogen surveillance and One Health research.
papers.abstract: Launched in 2024, gcPathogen established a critical foundation for the genomic surveillance of human pathogens. Here, we present gcPathogen 2.0, a major multi-omics update designed to address key analytical bottlenecks, including the integration of genomic and transcriptional profiles, systematic tracking of cross-habitat distribution, and large-scale discovery of antimicrobial peptides (AMPs). This release expands coverage from 1134 to 1506 pathogenic species, spanning 557 bacteria, 508 fungi, 258 viruses, and 183 parasites, and increases total genomic records past 2.3 million. By incorporati
papers.summary: gcPathogen 2.0 is a major multi-omics expansion of a pathogen surveillance database, growing from 1,134 to 1,506 pathogenic species and exceeding 2.3 million genomic records. It adds transcriptional profiles, cross-habitat distribution tracking, and large-scale antimicrobial peptide discovery to support One Health research. The resource aims to address analytical bottlenecks in integrating genomic and transcriptomic data for global pathogen surveillance.

papers.title: Metabolomics Subcenter (Met-SC): an integrated metabolomics database and analysis platform.
papers.abstract: The rapid growth of metabolomics data has increased the need for integrated storage, analysis, and reuse. Here, we present Metabolomics Subcenter (Met-SC) V1.0 (https://metabolomics.dicp.ac.cn/), an integrated database and platform for standardized data deposition, spectral-resource management, online analysis, and disease-focused knowledge mining. The deposition framework captures project, sample, pretreatment, and instrument metadata across chromatographic, capillary electrophoresis-mass spectrometry, and nuclear magnetic resonance workflows. Met-SC contains 7  756  867 reference spectra ass
papers.summary: Met-SC is a new integrated metabolomics database and analysis platform that standardizes data deposition, manages spectral resources, and supports online analysis and disease-focused knowledge mining. It captures detailed metadata across LC-MS, CE-MS, and NMR workflows and contains over 7.7 million reference spectra, addressing the growing need for integrated storage and reuse of metabolomics data.

papers.title: Conversational Multi-Agentic Network-Driven Disease Module Identification and Drug Repurposing Prediction With ChatDRex: Platform Development Study.
papers.abstract: Repurposing approved drugs offers a time- and cost-effective alternative to traditional drug development. However, in silico prediction of repurposing candidates is challenging and requires the effective collaboration of specialists in various fields, including pharmacology, medicine, biology, and bioinformatics. Fragmented, specialized algorithms and tools often address only narrow aspects of the overall problem. Heterogeneous, unstructured data landscapes require the expertise of specialized users. Hence, diverse data sources might not integrate smoothly across workflows.
papers.summary: ChatDRex is a conversational multi-agent platform that combines network-based disease module identification with drug repurposing prediction, letting users interact with specialized AI agents through natural language. It aims to integrate fragmented tools and heterogeneous data sources into a single workflow, lowering the barrier for cross-disciplinary repurposing analyses. The paper describes the platform's development rather than reporting a validated repurposing discovery.

papers.title: InterPro: the protein sequence classification resource in 2027.
papers.abstract: InterPro (https://www.ebi.ac.uk/interpro) is a freely accessible resource for the classification of protein sequences. It integrates predictive models, known as signatures, from multiple member databases to classify sequences into families and to predict the presence of domains and functionally important sites. The InterPro database provides annotations for hundreds of millions of sequences, ensuring extensive coverage of UniProtKB, the standard repository of protein sequences, and includes mapping to several other major resources, such as Gene Ontology, the Protein Data Bank in Europe (PDBe),
papers.summary: InterPro is a freely accessible database that classifies protein sequences by integrating predictive models (signatures) from multiple member databases to assign proteins to families and identify domains and functional sites. The 2027 update provides annotations for hundreds of millions of sequences with extensive UniProtKB coverage and mappings to resources like Gene Ontology and PDBe. It remains a core reference resource for protein functional annotation.

papers.title: Integration of single-cell multi-omic data with graph-based topic modelling.
papers.abstract: Recent advances in single-cell biology enable the profiling of multiple molecular layers, such as the transcriptome, epigenome, and surface proteins, within a single cell. Tackling the complexity of these data from multiple perspectives allows researchers to gain the most comprehensive insights into cellular biological properties. Here, we propose a graph-based topic modelling method called bionSBM. Our method leverages well-known community-detection methods for multipartite graphs and the interpretability of topic modelling to cluster and explain high-dimensional, sparse, and noisy single-cel
papers.summary: The authors present bionSBM, a graph-based topic modelling method for integrating single-cell multi-omic data across transcriptome, epigenome, and surface protein layers. It combines community-detection algorithms for multipartite graphs with topic modelling to cluster and interpret high-dimensional, sparse, and noisy single-cell data. The approach aims to give researchers a unified, interpretable view of cellular properties from multiple molecular perspectives.

papers.title: Functional Analysis of GarCIPK8 from Gossypium aridum Conferring Salt Stress Tolerance in Gossypium hirsutum.
papers.abstract: Soil salinization is a major abiotic stress factor restricting global agricultural production. The CBL-CIPK signaling network, comprising calcineurin B-like proteins (CBLs) and CBL-interacting protein kinases (CIPKs), plays a critical role in plant adaptation to salt stress. Here, we focused on GarCIPK8, a CIPK gene previously isolated from the diploid wild cotton Gossypium aridum, and generated its overexpressing transgenic lines in G. hirsutum through Agrobacterium-mediated transformation. Under 300 mmol/L NaCl treatment, transgenic plants showed markedly enhanced growth performance, with gr
papers.summary: The authors overexpressed GarCIPK8, a CBL-interacting protein kinase gene from the salt-tolerant wild cotton Gossypium aridum, in cultivated upland cotton (G. hirsutum). Transgenic plants showed markedly improved growth under high-salinity (300 mM NaCl) conditions, indicating that GarCIPK8 enhances salt stress tolerance. This supports the CBL-CIPK signaling network as a target for engineering abiotic stress tolerance in crops.

papers.title: Crystalline silica particles exposure modulated miRNA expression profiles in human macrophage-like THP-1 cells.
papers.abstract: Occupational and environmental exposure to crystalline silica particles is a major global health concern linked to silicosis, pulmonary fibrosis, autoimmune disease, and lung cancer. MicroRNAs (miRNAs) regulate gene expression post-transcriptionally and are emerging as potential effect biomarkers of exposure in human biomonitoring studies. To identify intracellular and extracellular miRNAs responses to silica-particle exposure in human THP-1 derived macrophages, differentiated THP-1 derived macrophages were exposed to 0-300 µg/mL crystalline silica particles for 24 h. Cytotoxicity was assessed
papers.summary: This study profiled miRNA expression changes in human macrophage-like THP-1 cells after exposure to crystalline silica particles, identifying both intracellular and extracellular (secreted) miRNA responses. The findings suggest that specific miRNAs could serve as biomarkers of silica exposure in human biomonitoring. The work is preliminary, based on a single cell line and in vitro exposure, with functional consequences not yet established.

papers.title: Development of a Knowledge Map for Managing Symptoms of Graft-Versus-Host Disease in Patients Undergoing Hematopoietic Stem Cell Transplantation.
papers.abstract: Graft-versus-host disease (GVHD) remains a critical complication affecting patients undergoing hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT), with multifaceted symptoms requiring systematic management. Current clinical practices lack structured tools to guide nurses in addressing GVHD-related symptoms across diverse organ systems. This review aims to synthesize evidence on GVHD symptom management to construct a knowledge graph, enhancing nursing interventions and improving patient outcomes.
papers.summary: This review synthesizes evidence on managing graft-versus-host disease (GVHD) symptoms after hematopoietic stem cell transplantation to build a knowledge graph for nursing interventions. The goal is to provide a structured tool that helps nurses address GVHD symptoms across multiple organ systems, addressing a gap in current clinical practice.

papers.title: Cutibacterium acnes induces T-cell extracellular traps with distinct proteome programs.
papers.abstract: Cutibacterium acnes is a common skin commensal associated with acne pathogenesis. In this study, we investigated whether acne-associated (denoted as CA) (HL043PA1) and healthy skin-associated (denoted as CH) (HL110PA3) C acnes strains differentially induce extracellular traps (ETs) in human neutrophils (neutrophil ETs) and T helper 17 cells (T-cell ETs [TETs]) and defined their proteomic and functional properties. Both strains triggered rapid ET release from neutrophils and T helper 17 cells. However, whereas neutrophil ETs displayed a conserved proteomic profile regardless of the strain, TETs
papers.summary: This study shows that both acne-associated and healthy skin-associated strains of Cutibacterium acnes trigger rapid extracellular trap release from human neutrophils and Th17 cells. While neutrophil extracellular traps had a conserved proteomic profile regardless of strain, T-cell extracellular traps displayed distinct proteome programs depending on the C. acnes strain, suggesting strain-specific functional consequences in acne pathogenesis.

papers.title: Reactive astrocyte subpopulations with high Gfap and C4b expression in different Alzheimer's disease mouse models: Single-cell nuclear transcriptome analysis.
papers.abstract: Understanding the cellular landscape underlying the heterogeneity of Alzheimer’s disease and the cell type-specific molecular perturbations is essential for identifying novel, targeted therapeutic strategies. However, previous bulk transcriptomic studies have failed to capture the unique contributions of individual cell populations to the early pathogenesis of the disease, and the functional diversity of key cell types in driving Alzheimer’s disease progression remains insufficiently characterized. In this study, we examined transcriptional changes in hippocampal tissue during early Alzheimer’
papers.summary: This study used single-nucleus RNA sequencing to profile hippocampal tissue from multiple Alzheimer's disease mouse models during early disease stages, revealing reactive astrocyte subpopulations characterized by high Gfap and C4b expression. The work highlights astrocyte heterogeneity across different AD models and identifies cell-type-specific molecular perturbations that bulk transcriptomics could not resolve. These findings may inform targeted therapeutic strategies aimed at specific reactive astrocyte states.

papers.title: Reframing QSP: AI-Driven Multi-Modal Data as a New Measurement Layer.
papers.abstract: Quantitative systems pharmacology (QSP) provides a mechanistic framework for integrating biological and pharmacological knowledge in drug development. Simultaneously, advances in artificial intelligence (AI), particularly in multi-modal data analysis, are transforming how biological information is derived. I argue that AI should not be viewed as a data integration tool, but as a new layer of quantitative measurement generation. This reframing positions QSP as a foundational model of biology, used here in a conceptual rather than technical sense, and AI as a source of quantitative inputs.
papers.summary: This perspective argues that AI should be reframed not as a tool for integrating data into quantitative systems pharmacology (QSP) models, but as a new layer that generates quantitative measurements from multi-modal biological data. Under this view, QSP serves as a conceptual foundational model of biology, while AI supplies the quantitative inputs that feed it. The piece is a conceptual/opinion contribution rather than a primary research study.

papers.title: PDBe-SIFTS: An open-source tool for Structure Integration with Function, Taxonomy, and Sequences, featuring improved alignment, scoring scheme, and accelerated search.
papers.abstract: Structure integration with function, taxonomy and sequences (SIFTS) provides residue-level mappings between UniProt Knowledgebase sequences and Protein Data Bank structures and has historically been generated through internal Protein Data Bank in Europe (PDBe) pipelines. Here, PDBe-SIFTS is presented as a fully open-source, locally deployable implementation of this mapping framework. The pipeline combines fast, scalable sequence search using MMseqs2, an improved bounded scoring scheme for ranking candidate mappings, and residue-level mapping refinement based on backbone connectivity. PDBe-SIFT
papers.journal: Protein science : a publication of the Protein Society
papers.summary: PDBe-SIFTS is a new open-source, locally deployable tool that maps residues between UniProt protein sequences and Protein Data Bank structures. It uses the fast MMseqs2 search engine, an improved scoring scheme for ranking candidate mappings, and backbone-connectivity-based refinement to produce accurate residue-level mappings. This makes the previously internal PDBe pipeline available to the broader community for local use.

papers.title: EXPERT: A practical and forward-looking guide to capturing protein expression and purification metadata to develop machine learning models.
papers.abstract: As machine learning (ML) becomes increasingly important in protein engineering, synthetic biology, and bioprocess optimization, the lack of consistent, complete, and standardized experimental reporting remains a major barrier to building effective models. EXPERT (EXpression and Purification Experimental Reporting Template) defines a structured framework for capturing protein expression and purification data across the community, to increase reproducibility across laboratories and support downstream ML applications. We propose here the essential data that should be recorded during expression an
papers.summary: The authors propose EXPERT, a standardized template for recording protein expression and purification metadata, addressing the lack of consistent experimental reporting that hampers machine learning in protein engineering and synthetic biology. By defining essential data fields to capture across laboratories, the framework aims to improve reproducibility and enable the construction of effective ML models from aggregated experimental data.

papers.title: Single-cell chromatin accessibility atlas decodes bone development, diseases, and regeneration.
papers.abstract: Bone development, homeostasis, and regeneration are governed by complex, dynamic gene regulatory programs, and these processes are disrupted in numerous skeletal diseases. The epigenetic landscape-particularly chromatin accessibility-dictates transcription factor binding and gene expression, which fundamentally shape bone cell fate and function. In recent years, single-cell chromatin accessibility technologies, most notably single-cell assay for transposase-accessible chromatin using sequencing (scATAC-seq), have revolutionized bone epigenome research and enabled single-cell resolution dissect
papers.summary: This review synthesizes how single-cell chromatin accessibility technologies, especially scATAC-seq, have been applied to decode the epigenetic regulatory programs underlying bone development, skeletal disease, and regeneration. It highlights how chromatin accessibility maps reveal transcription factor binding dynamics that control bone cell fate and function at single-cell resolution.

papers.title: Comparative Transcriptomic and Physiological Profiling Reveals Species-Associated Differences Across Five Duckweed Species.
papers.abstract: Duckweeds (Lemnaceae) are fast-growing aquatic monocots with potential for biomass production and phytoremediation, but baseline molecular and physiological differences among species remain poorly characterized. We assembled de novo transcriptomes of five duckweed species, Lemna minor, Lemna japonica, Lemna gibba, Landoltia punctata, and Lemna aequinoctialis, grown on basal Murashige and Skoog (MS) medium (three biological replicates per species), and evaluated for completeness with Benchmarking Universal Single-Copy Orthologs (BUSCO) against Viridiplantae, Embryophyta, and Liliopsida referenc
papers.summary: The authors assembled de novo transcriptomes for five duckweed species and compared them alongside physiological measurements, using BUSCO to assess assembly completeness. This provides a baseline resource characterizing molecular and physiological differences among species with potential for biomass production and phytoremediation.

papers.title: A Traditional Chinese Medicine Knowledge Graph for Hypertension With Emotional Comorbidity: Development and Blinded Question-Answering Evaluation.
papers.abstract: Traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) literature on hypertension with anxiety, depression, or insomnia contains descriptions of syndrome patterns, treatment principles, formulas, and herbs. A focused knowledge graph can organize these associations and their sources, but its contribution to generated answers requires separate evaluation.
papers.summary: This paper develops a knowledge graph that organizes Traditional Chinese Medicine concepts—syndrome patterns, treatment principles, formulas, and herbs—for hypertension with emotional comorbidities such as anxiety, depression, and insomnia, while preserving source citations. It then evaluates whether grounding generated answers in this graph improves question-answering quality using a blinded assessment. The work demonstrates a domain-specific approach to structuring TCM literature for retrieval-augmented clinical question answering.

papers.title: Dingent: A Configurable Agent Framework for Biological Database Retrieval and Integration.
papers.abstract: Natural-language retrieval across biological databases requires resource-specific tools, model instructions, and coordinated query steps. We present Dingent, an open-source agent framework that composes resource-specific tools into explicit multistep retrieval paths, integrating data-access plugins, configurable assistants, directed workflows, and web interfaces. Within this framework, developers expose resource functions as tools, administrators configure assistants and workflows, and users query the resulting application in natural language. We compared Dingent with a single-assistant tool-c
papers.summary: Dingent is an open-source agent framework that lets developers wrap biological database functions as tools, configure assistants and directed multi-step workflows, and expose the result through web interfaces for natural-language querying. It aims to make cross-database retrieval and integration more reproducible and configurable than a single general-purpose assistant, and the authors benchmark it against that baseline.

papers.title: PhageLysData: an evidence-aware and AI-ready dataset of phage lytic enzymes and depolymerases.
papers.abstract: Bacteriophage lytic enzymes and depolymerases are relevant to phage biology, antimicrobial development, and protein engineering, but their sequence and annotation data remain dispersed across general databases, specialized resources, genome-centred collections, and prediction-oriented datasets. We present PhageLysData, an evidence-aware and AI-ready resource constructed through reproducible multisource integration, provenance tracking, and exact-sequence consolidation. The release integrates 807,366 source observations from seven primary resources into 759,105 unique exact-sequence entities, c
papers.summary: PhageLysData integrates seven primary data sources into a consolidated, provenance-tracked resource of 759,105 unique phage lytic enzyme and depolymerase sequences from 807,366 source observations. The dataset is designed to be evidence-aware and AI-ready, supporting research in phage biology, antimicrobial development, and protein engineering.

papers.title: Advancing FAIR data management through AI-assisted curation of morphological data matrices.
papers.abstract: Curation of biological and paleontological datasets is a labor-intensive process that requires standardization and validation to ensure data integrity. In particular, manual curation of datasets is prone to human errors such as typographical errors, inconsistent formatting, and incomplete metadata, which hinder reproducibility and compliance with Findability, Accessibility, Interoperability, and Reusability (FAIR) principles. Artificial Intelligence (AI) offers a transformative solution for enhancing research efficiency by automating data validation, improving accuracy, and streamlining curati
papers.summary: This paper presents an AI-assisted approach to curating morphological data matrices, automating validation tasks like detecting typographical errors, inconsistent formatting, and incomplete metadata. The method aims to improve compliance with FAIR data principles and reduce manual curation effort in biological and paleontological datasets. It demonstrates how AI can streamline data standardization and validation workflows.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence as a Multifaceted Toolkit for Antibacterial Drug Discovery against Resistance.
papers.abstract: How artificial intelligence (AI) can be rationally applied to antibacterial drug discovery and development to overcome antimicrobial resistance (AMR) remains insufficiently defined, particularly across different resistance mechanisms and translational stages. The global emergence and dissemination of AMR are compromising conventional antibacterial therapies, while slow antibiotic discovery, limited target diversity, and reliance on single-mechanism drug design further increase the risk of inadequate treatment options. With strengths in multi-omics integration, complex pattern recognition, and
papers.summary: This review argues that AI can serve as a multifaceted toolkit across the antibacterial drug discovery pipeline to combat antimicrobial resistance, spanning target identification, compound screening, and drug design. It emphasizes integrating multi-omics data and complex pattern recognition to address slow discovery and limited target diversity. The paper frames AI application across different resistance mechanisms and translational stages, though the abstract is truncated.
